<reason>Side B won a close debate by forcing a cleaner decision rule: with no basin referee, treating Egypt’s live drought objection as a stop on Ethiopia’s remaining timetable is a veto with no off-switch. CON’s survival-versus-delayed-power weighing and wet-year versus successive-drought distinction were serious, and CON correctly damaged the claim that turbines make holdbacks irrational. But CON never operationalized a non-veto constraint, hedged the required yes/no on whether Cairo’s refusal halts filling, and left PRO’s “who decides when there is no agreement” clash standing. PRO answered pressure more directly and kept the proposition’s default internally consistent.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s “dam you may build but may not fill is a wall” frame, which turned CON’s drought-hold into a functional veto after CON’s A4.1 concession that Ethiopia may not proceed on its remaining timetable while Egypt’s objection is live.</best_rebuttal>
